receipt.public_excerpt: Despite its capabilities, GPT‑4 has similar limitations as earlier GPT models. Most importantly, it still is not fully reliable (it “hallucinates” facts and makes reasoning errors).

evidence_items.explanation: The leading lab says its flagship model, released within the period, still hallucinates and is not fully reliable.

evidence_items.locator: section About those odd results, paragraph 3

receipt.public_excerpt: But some odd, inaccurate or unhelpful AI Overviews certainly did show up.

evidence_items.explanation: Days before the post, Google admitted its new AI search feature gave inaccurate answers at launch. This shows reliability problems were still present.

evidence_items.locator: section AI-Driven Legal Research Tools Still Hallucinate, paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: even these bespoke legal AI tools still hallucinate an alarming amount of the time: the Lexis+ AI and Ask Practical Law AI systems produced incorrect information more than 17% of the time, while Westlaw’s AI-Assisted Research hallucinated more than 34% of the time.

evidence_items.explanation: In May 2024, an independent test found that commercial tools built on LLMs and marketed as hallucination-free still hallucinated often.

receipt.public_excerpt: While still a real issue, GPT‑4 significantly reduces hallucinations relative to previous models (which have themselves been improving with each iteration).

evidence_items.explanation: This shows real progress in reducing hallucinations during the period. It does not show they were resolved; the same passage calls them 'still a real issue'.
